title: Producers, Consumers and Decomposers
seo_title: Year 4 Science: Producers, Consumers and Decomposers Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Explain the roles and interactions of consumers, producers and decomposers within a habitat and how food chains represent feeding relationships (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on producers, consumers and decomposers in Australian habitats: gum trees, koalas, dingoes, fungi, earthworms and dung beetles, and how matter is recycled. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Make food, eat food, break down.
key_sub: Producers make food, consumers eat it, decomposers recycle dead matter.
body_html:
How to think about it

Every living thing in a habitat has a role.

  • Producers (plants, algae, seagrass) make their own food using sunlight.
  • Consumers (animals) eat other living things for energy.
  • Decomposers (fungi, bacteria, earthworms, dung beetles) break down dead things and waste, returning nutrients to the soil.
Example

A mushroom grows on a log. Role?

it cannot make food from sunlight

it feeds on dead wood

Answer: decomposer

Example

A dugong eats seagrass. Role?

it eats another living thing

Answer: consumer

Common mistakes

  • Calling fungi such as mushrooms plants (they are decomposers).
  • Thinking decomposers are only pests that spoil food.
  • Thinking animals can make their own food.

faq.q: What is the difference between a producer and a consumer?
faq.a: A producer, such as a gum tree, makes its own food from sunlight. A consumer, such as a koala, gets its energy by eating other living things.
Fungi, bacteria, earthworms, slaters and dung beetles. They break down dead plants, animals and waste.
They recycle nutrients from dead matter back into the soil, so new plants can grow.
